title: Self JOIN
flavorText: A table can be joined to itself to compare rows within the same table. You MUST use aliases for this.
narrative: Find pairs of customers who share the same tier.
schemaSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, tier TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, status TEXT NOT NULL, total REAL NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE order_items (order_id INTEGER, product_id INTEGER, quantity INTEGER);
seedSql: INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','Gold'),(2,'Bob','Silver'),(3,'Charlie','Bronze'),(4,'Diana','Gold'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (101,1,'Shipped',150.0),(102,2,'Pending',80.0),(103,1,'Delivered',200.0),(104,NULL,'Cancelled',50.0); INSERT INTO products VALUES (10,'Widget',25.0),(20,'Gizmo',50.0),(30,'Doodad',10.0); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (101,10,2),(101,20,2),(102,10,1),(102,30,5),(103,20,4);
task: Join the customers table to itself. Select c1.name as name1 and c2.name as name2 where they have the same tier, but are NOT the same customer (c1.id < c2.id to avoid duplicates). Order by name1, then name2.

hints.text: FROM customers c1 JOIN customers c2 ON c1.tier = c2.tier
Add WHERE c1.id < c2.id to prevent matching a customer with themselves, and to prevent A-B and B-A duplicates.
SELECT c1.name AS name1, c2.name AS name2 FROM customers c1 JOIN customers c2 ON c1.tier = c2.tier WHERE c1.id < c2.id ORDER BY name1, name2;
